cand.title: 2027 National Bank Open presented by Rogers — Toronto
cand.excerpt: International professional tennis tournament scheduled for July 31–August 12, 2027, with the ATP component in Toronto. Visiting players, coaches, officials, media and spectators create a credible multi-day lodging window, but no room block is asserted.
linkedLedgerProgrammes: Tennis Canada — 2027 National Bank Open presented by Rogers — Toronto

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two verified commercial/event influencers: Rob Swann, VP, Chief Commercial Officer, Tennis Canada, responsible for corporate partnerships and stadium sales revenue for both NBO tournaments; Karl Hale, Toronto Tournament Director, National Bank Open. Neither source establishes hotel procurement or contract-signing authority. Tennis Canada publishes csavard@tenniscanada.com for partnership opportunities; use it as a routing channel, not a verified housing desk.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced upcoming Toronto ATP edition: July 31–August 12, 2027. These are activity dates, not publication dates. The official guide specifies qualifying July 31, first-round matches August 1, and finals August 12. The ticket page cautions: “Dates are subject to change.” This is within the requested horizon.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: a 157-room Harbourfront city hotel is not a sole housing solution for this large tournament. Stadium access is the principal weakness: play is at York University, not near the hotel’s downtown/MTCC territory. Conditional niches are small sponsor/VIP groups, downtown-preferring spectators, selected media/executive stays or ancillary meetings, only after transport and buyer preferences are confirmed. A roughly 15–109-peak-room proposal would be a sales-sizing scenario, NOT published event demand. Resort positioning offers no evidenced advantage. Do not promise restaurant, lounge, reception catering or full player/team housing.
findings.venueCommitments: Sobeys Stadium, York University campus, 1 Shoreham Drive, Toronto, Ontario M3N 3A6. Official 2027 material identifies Sobeys Stadium in Toronto. It is in Toronto proper, in the north of the city, NOT Harbourfront/downtown, MTCC or Exhibition Place. This is an announced sporting venue, not a hotel commitment or evidence of lodging availability.
findings.historicalRotation: Verified Toronto editions: ATP August 5–13, 2023; WTA August 4–12, 2024; ATP July 26–August 7, 2025 (qualifying July 26); WTA August 1–13, 2026 (qualifying August 1). All use Sobeys Stadium. The 2027 guide explicitly returns ATP to Toronto and WTA to Montreal. This is alternating tour/city programming, not evidence that the Toronto event rotates to downtown venues. No later Toronto dates are asserted.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Official Toronto accommodation page states: “The Hilton, the official hotel partner of the tournament, has two locations ready to welcome you during your visit.” EVERY hotel on that official Toronto page: Homewood Suites by Hilton Vaughan (from CAD 279/night plus taxes; “Please ask for the National Bank Open General public rate”; 1-905-760-1660) and Home2 Suites Vaughan Toronto (from CAD 255/night plus taxes; “Please ask for the Sports Elite discount”; 1-905-605-9608). This establishes a published official-partner referral/rate pathway. The accommodation body has no edition-specific stay dates, inventory, cutoff or signed block terms; the site’s 2027 schedule banner alone does not establish a 2027 room-block commitment. No public housing-bureau appointment, procurement owner, open lodging RFP or 2027 contracted room allocation was verified. Separately, Championship Tennis Tours offers custom spectator packages: “Based on the availability we’ll always try to include your top pick in the firm quote we send you.” The retrieved package form lists Courtyard by Marriott Toronto Vaughan; Residence Inn by Marriott Vaughn; Springhill Suites; Hotel Le Germain Mercer; The Drake; Doubletree Hotel Downtown; Shangri La Hotel; Fairmont Royal York; Park Hyatt Toronto; Ritz Carlton - Toronto. These are third-party featured choices, NOT official incumbent hotels or guaranteed inventory.
findings.organizationStructure: Tennis Canada describes itself as a non-profit national sport association and explicitly says it owns and operates the National Bank Open ATP and WTA events. National Bank and Rogers are tournament branding/sponsorship identities, not the researched hotel buyer. Sobeys Stadium is the sporting venue; no appointed PCO, DMC or independent housing bureau was verified. Championship Tennis Tours is a separate spectator-package seller, not established as Tennis Canada’s lodging procurer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Hilton already has official hotel-partner positioning and the official Toronto page actively refers guests to two Vaughan properties. This is an incumbent distribution advantage, not proof that all 2027 lodging is exclusive or contracted elsewhere. No sourced hotel sell-out, overflow requirement, rejected block or unmet room demand was found. Historical Toronto attendance was 217,531 in 2025 and 215,872 in 2026; these are tournament-wide attendance counts, not peak attendance, unique out-of-town guests or rooms. No 2027 attendance forecast, peak-room count or event room-night total was verified.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Tennis Canada through its published partnership channel, requesting routing to Rob Swann and the actual Toronto accommodation/operations owner; use Karl Hale for Toronto event alignment. First ask whether 2027 hotel commitments include exclusivity, which traveler cohorts remain unallocated, whether a downtown satellite is welcome, who procures it and when the next competitive cycle opens. Only then offer a modest, non-exclusive Radisson room proposal with an explicit north-Toronto transport plan. Confirm dates of stay, peak rooms, room nights and hotel catering operations before pricing or promising meetings. If 2027 is closed, request the next announced Toronto sourcing window rather than inventing a future edition date.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the upcoming 2027 edition, tickets are on sale but lodging procurement accessibility is unconfirmed. Public partner hotel rates do not constitute an invitation to competing hotels. The prior SALES_READY label is not substantiated: retain a conditional relationship-development lead rather than an open group-room opportunity. There is no evidence that Radisson has an allocation, buyer invitation or genuine overflow request.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: future recurring Toronto editions could support a non-exclusive downtown ancillary-hotel relationship, contingent on Hilton rights, transport, actual downtown preference and sourcing timing. The evidence supports recurring Toronto activity and a confirmed 2027 edition, NOT future unannounced dates, a movable host venue, an expiring hotel agreement or a guaranteed competitive tender. Seek a small complementary role rather than displacement of official hotels.
